items.title: Trump says Cuba negotiating deal at Miami summit

featured_image.name: Trump says Cuba negotiating deal with him and Rubio | Reuters

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that Cuba is actively negotiating a deal with the United States, making the announcement at the "Shield of the Americas" summit in Miami, where he gathered leaders from across Latin America. Trump said Cuba is "at the end of the line" and that discussions are underway with him and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.[1]

"They are looking to negotiate, and they are in talks with Marco, myself, and several others. I believe that a deal could be easily established with Cuba," Trump said at the event held at Trump National Doral. The remarks escalate weeks of mounting pressure on Havana and follow Trump telling CNN on Friday that Cuba "is going to fall pretty soon," adding that he plans to "put Marco over there" to handle the situation.[2][1]

items.title: Iran fires 7 missile barrages at Israel as war enters second week

featured_image.name: Photos show Iran launching missile counterattack on Israel

items.description: Iran launched at least seven waves of ballistic missiles targeting central Israel since midnight Saturday, triggering air raid sirens across Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, and surrounding areas as the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran entered its second week with no signs of abating.

items.title: Guinea dissolves 40 political parties, including top opposition groups

featured_image.name: Guinea Dissolves 40 Political Parties, Including Main ...

items.description:
Guinea's government dissolved 40 political parties in a late-night decree issued Friday, stripping the country's three main opposition groups of their legal status less than two months after former junta leader Mamady Doumbouya was sworn in as president. The Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation, Ibrahima Kalil Condé, ordered the dissolutions for "failure to fulfil their obligations," according to the decree broadcast on state television.[1][2]

Among the disbanded parties are the Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea (UFDG), led by exiled former prime minister Cellou Dalein Diallo; the Rally of the Guinean People (RPG), the party of ousted former president Alpha Condé; and the Union of Republican Forces (UFR), founded by another exiled former prime minister, Sidya Touré.[3][4][5]

items.title: Dubai airport resumes flights after Iranian drone explodes near terminal

featured_image.name: Chaos at Dubai airport after flights suspended following ...

items.description:
Dubai International Airport, the world's busiest hub for international travel, was forced to temporarily halt all flight operations on Saturday morning after an Iranian drone exploded in close proximity to one of its terminal buildings, marking the second time in a week that the airport has come under direct threat from Tehran's retaliatory strikes on Gulf states.

Emirates, the Middle East's largest airline, announced in a post on X that all flights to and from Dubai were suspended until further notice, urging passengers not to travel to the airport. The carrier resumed operations by early afternoon local time, advising only passengers with confirmed bookings to proceed to the airport.[1][2]

items.title: Trump threatens expanded strikes on Iran as war enters second week

featured_image.name: Trump hasn't decided whether to strike Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump warned Saturday that Iran "will be hit very hard" and said the United States is considering striking "areas and groups of people that were not considered for targeting up until this moment in time," a sharp escalation in rhetoric as the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its eighth day with no end in sight.[1]

"Today Iran will be hit very hard!" Trump wrote in a social media post in the early hours of Saturday, adding that attacks would continue "until they surrender or, more likely, completely collapse!" In a separate post, he cited Iran's "bad behavior" as justification for giving "serious consideration for complete destruction and certain death" to previously untargeted areas.[1]

items.title: UAE president declares 'we are no easy prey' as Iranian strikes enter second week

featured_image.name: Watch: UAE President visits victims of recent attacks receiving hospital treatment

items.description:
UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan declared his country was "in a period of war" but resilient, delivering his first public remarks since Iran began launching missiles and drones at the Gulf state over a week ago. "The UAE has thick skin and bitter flesh — we are no easy prey," he said during a visit to wounded civilians at Sheikh Shakhbout Medical City in Abu Dhabi on Friday, according to comments broadcast on Abu Dhabi TV on Saturday.[1][2][3]

The Emirati leader, who also serves as ruler of Abu Dhabi, praised the role of citizens and the military and pledged to protect everyone living in the federation. "We will carry out our duty towards our country, our people, and our residents who are also part of our family," he said. He spoke with injured individuals and their families from the UAE, Sudan, Iran, Pakistan, and India, reassuring them "they are among their family in the UAE".[4][2]

items.title: Turkey weighs deploying F-16 jets to Northern Cyprus

featured_image.name: Iran War: Turkey Weighs F-16 Deployment to Northern Cyprus ...

items.description:
Turkey is weighing the deployment of F-16 fighter jets to Northern Cyprus as the fallout from the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran continues to reshape the eastern Mediterranean security landscape.

Turkish Defense Ministry sources confirmed Saturday that "phased planning is underway to ensure the security of the TRNC," adding that "the deployment of F-16 aircraft to the island is among the options being considered," according to Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency. Reuters separately reported the move is part of a series of measures aimed at safeguarding the self-declared Turkish Cypriot state as tensions rise in the region. Bloomberg also reported that Turkey was considering deploying F-16 warplanes to bolster northern Cypriot defenses.[1][2][3]

items.title: Protests erupt across Havana after days without power

featured_image.name: Cuba hit by massive power outage amid US oil pressure - Al Jazeera

items.description:
Nighttime protests broke out across Havana on Friday, March 6, as Cubans endured what some reported as more than 60 hours without electricity following the collapse of the country's National Electric System earlier in the week. Residents in Centro Habana, Vedado, Marianao, La Habana Vieja, and San Miguel del Padrón banged pots and pans and shouted slogans in the darkness, according to videos circulating on social media.[1][2]

The demonstrations mark the latest eruption of public anger on an island caught between a crumbling power grid and an intensifying U.S. campaign to cut off its fuel supplies. Analyst Thomas van Linge reported on X that "protests against the communist regime are now being reported in several neighborhoods across the capital" after residents spent more than 60 hours without power. Spain's El Mundo reported that the energy crisis reached one of its worst points on Friday, with roughly 70% of the island left in the dark.[2][1]

items.title: Balen Shah's party heads for landslide in Nepal's post-protest election

featured_image.name: Nepal's rapper-mayor Balen Shah surges ahead in polls with Gen Z ...

items.description:
Rapper-turned-politician Balendra Shah's Rastriya Swatantra Party is heading toward a sweeping victory in Nepal's general elections, upending decades of dominance by the country's traditional political establishment. As of Saturday, the RSP had won 20 seats and was leading in 98 others out of 165 directly elected constituencies in the 275-member House of Representatives, according to the latest Election Commission data reported by NDTV.[1]

Shah, 35, delivered the most dramatic result of the election by unseating four-time former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli in his own stronghold of Jhapa-5. According to final results from the constituency, Shah received 68,348 votes to Oli's 18,734 — a margin of 49,614 votes. The RSP also took the lead in all constituencies across the Kathmandu Valley and made deep inroads in other provinces.[2][3][4]

items.title: Over 200 metabolic enzymes found on human DNA, study reveals

featured_image.name: Tracking the metabolic origins of cancer from a mosaic of cells

items.description: More than two hundred metabolic enzymes — many of which were thought to operate exclusively in the mitochondria — have been found sitting directly on human DNA inside the cell nucleus, according to a study published March 6 in Nature Communications. The finding reveals that each cell type, tissue, and cancer harbors a distinct "nuclear metabolic fingerprint," opening a new front in understanding how tumors grow and resist treatment.[1]

items.title: IRGC strikes eighth vessel as Hormuz oil traffic drops to zero

featured_image.name: Oil supertanker rates hit all-time high as Iran pledges to close the Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran has paralyzed one of the world's most critical shipping corridors, halting oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and sending shockwaves through global energy markets and supply chains now entering a second week.

As of Wednesday, the number of oil tankers passing through the strait — a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that normally carries roughly 20 percent of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas — had dropped to zero, down from 37 vessels the day before hostilities began on February 28, according to Reuters. On March 7, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps struck yet another commercial vessel, a Malta-flagged tanker, bringing the total number of ships hit to at least eight.[1][2]

items.title: Oil posts strongest weekly gain since 2022 as Hormuz stays shut

featured_image.name: Oil and natural gas surge after Iran orders Strait of Hormuz closure

items.description: The week-long U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran has sent global oil and liquefied petroleum gas prices sharply higher, with crude benchmarks posting their strongest weekly gains since 2022 as the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint for roughly 20% of the world's oil supply — remains effectively closed to commercial shipping.[1][2][3]

items.title: Reports: Israel used Blue Sparrow missile to kill Khamenei

featured_image.name: Iran's Ayatollah Ali Khamenei is killed in Israeli strike, ending 36-year iron rule

items.description: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed on February 28 in a joint U.S.-Israeli airstrike on his compound in Tehran, in what Israel dubbed Operation Roaring Lion. Reports now indicate that among the weapons deployed was the Blue Sparrow, an Israeli air-launched ballistic missile that briefly exits the atmosphere before plunging nearly vertically onto its target at hypersonic speed.

items.title: Mideast war widens as Iran missiles hit Tel Aviv, Gulf states intercept strikes

featured_image.name: Smaller volleys, more alerts: Attacking Israel anew, Iran ...

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced this week that its hypersonic missiles and advanced drones bypassed the US-made THAAD missile defense system and struck targets in central Israel, including the Israeli Defense Ministry building and Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv, according to the IRGC's statement carried by Iranian state news agency IRNA. The claims, which Israel has disputed, came as a Chinese research paper published days earlier predicted that US missile defenses were "dangerously outmatched" by hypersonic threats — an assessment that footage from the conflict appeared to support.[1]

items.title: Chinese study on US missile defense gaps validated by Iran war, analysts say

featured_image.name: Iran claims it has hypersonic missile

items.description: As the US-Israeli war on Iran enters its second week, Iran's deployment of hypersonic missiles has exposed vulnerabilities in some of the world's most advanced air defense systems — outcomes that a Chinese research team had predicted in a paper published before the conflict began.

items.title: ALMA finds high methanol levels in interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS

featured_image.name: Cometa interestelar 3I/ATLAS tem quantidade incomum de álcool | G1

items.description:
Astronomers using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) have discovered that interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS contains an unusually large amount of methanol, far exceeding what is typically found in comets born in our own solar system, according to new findings released by the National Radio Astronomy Observatory on March 6.[1][2]

The research, led by Nathan Roth of American University, reveals that 3I/ATLAS is one of the most methanol-rich comets ever studied — offering scientists a rare chemical fingerprint from another planetary system without ever leaving our own.

items.title: Trump demands Iran's 'unconditional surrender' as oil tops $90

featured_image.name: Donald Trump: No deal with Iran, unconditional surrender ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Friday that there will be "no deal" with Iran without its unconditional surrender, a demand that escalated fears of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East and sent global oil prices to their highest levels in more than two years.

"There will be no deal with Iran — UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER!" Trump wrote on social media, adding that after capitulation and "selection of a GREAT & ACCEPTABLE Leader(s)," the United States and its allies would help rebuild the country. The statement represents the most expansive articulation yet of the administration's war aims, now extending to explicit regime change, according to Politico, which reported that Trump told the outlet he plans to "have a big impact" in choosing Iran's next leader.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran's Guards dare US Navy to escort tankers through Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran's Guards challenges Trump to have US Navy escort oil ...

items.description:
A spokesperson for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Friday taunted President Trump over his pledge to escort oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, daring American forces to enter the contested waterway as the U.S.-Iran conflict enters its second week.

Brigadier General Ali Mohammad Naeini said Iran "strongly welcomes the escorting of oil tankers and the claimed presence of US forces to facilitate passage through the Strait of Hormuz," according to Iranian state media. "In fact, we are awaiting their arrival," he added.[1][2]

Naeini warned the United States to recall the 1987 Bridgeton incident, when an American supertanker struck an Iranian mine in the Persian Gulf while sailing under U.S. Navy escort during the Iran-Iraq War, "as well as tankers that have been targeted recently."[2][1]

items.title: Cuba shuts Quito embassy after Ecuador expels diplomats

featured_image.name: Cuba shuts its Quito embassy as Ecuador expels its diplomats ...

items.description:
Cuba's embassy in Quito ceased all operations on Friday after the 48-hour deadline set by Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa for all Cuban diplomatic personnel to leave the country expired. The Cuban flag was lowered from the embassy in northern Quito before staff departed, marking one of the sharpest diplomatic ruptures in Latin America in recent years.[1][2]

Ecuador's Ministry of Foreign Affairs declared Ambassador Basilio Antonio Gutiérrez García and the 22 members of his diplomatic, consular, and administrative staff persona non grata on March 4, citing Article 9 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations but offering no specific justification for the move. Noboa simultaneously revoked the credentials of Ecuador's own ambassador to Havana, José María Borja López.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: US military carries out lethal strikes in Ecuador

featured_image.name: Why did US launch military operations in Ecuador? Here's what we know

items.description:
The U.S. military on Friday confirmed it carried out lethal kinetic operations on the ground in Ecuador, marking a dramatic escalation from the advisory role American forces had played just days earlier and extending the Trump administration's militarized counter-narcotics campaign from sea to land for the first time in the country.

"At the request of Ecuador, the Department of War executed targeted action to advance our shared objective of dismantling narco-terrorist networks," Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell wrote on X. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth separately posted that U.S. forces were conducting strikes against "narco-terrorist sites on the ground" in partnership with Ecuador, adding, "Much more to come".[1][2]
